documents.text:
BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                        )
 EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR                               )
 REVISION OF ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES                      )   Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317                          )


SUA SPONTE ORDER VACATING PROCEDURAL SCHEDULE, TOLLING PENDING
  DEADLINES, AND REQUIRING THE FILING OF AN AMENDED APPLICATION

       THIS MATTER comes before the Hearing Examiner upon El Paso Electric Company’s

(“EPE”) Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates (“Application”), filed on March 27,

2026; EPE’s Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits, filed on April 15, 2026 (“First

Errata Notice”); EPE’s Second Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits, filed on July

7, 2026 (“Second Errata Notice”); and the Expedited Joint Objection and Motion for an Order

Rejecting EPE’s Second Notice of Errata and Staying the Procedural Schedule Pending the

Company’s Compliance with NMPRC Rule 1.2.2.10(G) NMAC (“Joint Objection”).

       Having reviewed the Application, EPE’s two errata notices, the motions and responses

identified above, and the procedural record, the Hearing Examiner concludes that the Application,

considered together with its supporting testimony, exhibits, schedules, and workpapers, was not

filed in a sufficiently complete, accurate, and reviewable form to permit this proceeding to continue

fairly and efficiently. The deficiencies at issue are procedural and documentary. This Order does

not resolve or prejudge the substantive merits of any requests made by EPE.

       For the reasons stated below, the current hearing and procedural schedule shall be vacated,

all pending motion and other deadlines tolled, and EPE shall be required to file, within twenty-one

calendar days, a single amended and restated Application and complete supporting filing package

(“Amended Application”). This is EPE’s one opportunity to present a complete, internally

consistent, and reviewable application in this docket. If the Amended Application does not satisfy
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


these requirements, the Hearing Examiner will recommend that the Application be dismissed

without prejudice, requiring EPE to initiate any renewed request for rate relief in a new docket.

           I.      PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND

1.         On March 27, 2026, EPE filed its Application seeking revision of its New Mexico retail

electric rates pursuant to Advice Notice No. 317. EPE defined the “Application” to include not

only the underlying pleading, but the entire rate-filing package, including testimony, exhibits, Rule

530 schedules, workpapers, proposed tariffs, Advice Notice No. 317, and other supporting

documents incorporated into the Application by reference.1

2.         EPE’s original filing comprised approximately 4,157 pages.

3.         On April 15, 2026, nineteen days after filing the Application and one day before the

scheduled prehearing conference, EPE filed the 1,657-page First Errata Notice.

4.         The First Errata Notice disclosed, among other matters, that:

           a. an exhibit identified as the qualifications of an EPE witness contained the wrong

                document;

           b. a table in another witness’s testimony required replacement because it was difficult to

                read;

           c. Schedule A-3 did not follow the correct format, contained information not required by

                the applicable filing rule, and was incorrectly labeled; and

           d. the original Application had omitted multiple categories of completed workpapers,

                including Workpapers A, G, H, J, K, M, and P.2




1
    EPE Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates (Mar. 27, 2026) at 1-2.
2
    EPE Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits (Apr. 15, 2026) at 1-2.

                                                       -2-
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


5.         By EPE’s own definition, the omitted workpapers formed part of the complete rate-filing

package and supported the schedules, testimony, proposed rates, and other relief presented for

Hearing Examiner review, and therefore were not peripheral documents.3

6.         On April 24, 2026, the Commission issued an Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317

and deemed the filing complete as of April 15, 2026, the date on which EPE filed the First Errata

Notice.4

7.         On April 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiner issued a Procedural Order establishing, among

other deadlines, July 24, 2026, as the deadline for Staff and intervenor direct testimony, August

19, 2026, as the deadline for rebuttal testimony, and September 21, 2026, as the commencement

date for the evidentiary hearing.5

8.         Thereafter, Staff and intervenors undertook discovery and began preparing their respective

analyses and testimony based upon the Application as supplemented by the First Errata Notice.

9.         On July 7, 2026, seventeen days before Staff and intervenor direct testimony was due, EPE

filed the Second Errata Notice.6

10.        The Second Errata Notice identified four additional categories of errors in workpapers

supporting the Application:

           a. amounts associated with allowance for funds used during construction and excess

               deferred taxes had been incorrectly inverted, and an amount of $33,440,078 allocated

               to one category should have been removed;



3
    EPE Application at 1–2; EPE First Errata Notice at 2.
4
    Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317 (April 24, 2026) at 6.
5
    Procedural Order (April 27, 2026) at 4-5.
6
    EPE Second Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits (July 7, 2026) at 1-2.

                                                       -3-
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


            b. several costs had been allocated to the New Mexico jurisdiction using a labor allocator

                  when, according to EPE, they should have been directly assigned to the New Mexico

                  jurisdiction;

            c. certain advertising expenses had been incorrectly coded to one Federal Energy

                  Regulatory Commission account rather than another and additional supporting

                  materials were required; and

            d. formulas and inputs used in an additional workpaper contained multiple errors,

                  including duplicated material costs and the use of incorrect employee-function values

                  in calculating overhead adders.7

11.         The Second Errata Notice did not include a revised cost-of-service study showing the

combined consequences of the corrections, a revised revenue requirement, revised proposed rates,

a revised set of affected schedules and testimony, or a comprehensive reconciliation identifying

every document and figure affected by the corrections.

12.         Instead, EPE stated that it “reserve[d] the right to further explain these corrections in

rebuttal testimony,” at which time it would file a revised cost of service reflecting the corrections.8

13.         The Joint Objection, filed July 10, 2026, identifies a series of specific facial

inconsistencies, omissions, and unanswered questions concerning the Second Errata Notice.

Among other things, the Joint Parties assert that:

            a. replacement Workpaper A-03, Adjustment No. 34R provides only Total Company

                  amounts, although the corresponding workpaper previously filed included both Total




7
    Id. at 1-2.
8
    Id. at 2.

                                                     -4-

Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


         Company and New Mexico jurisdictional amounts, thereby leaving the effect of the

         correction on EPE’s requested New Mexico revenue requirement unidentified;

      b. replacement Workpaper A-03, Adjustment No. 10R changes the New Mexico

         adjustment for regulatory commission expense from negative $146,056 to positive

         $665,102, an apparent difference of $811,158, without explaining the resulting effect

         on the revenue requirement, taxes, inspection and supervision fees, or proposed rates,

         while the detailed breakdown of regulatory expenses remains unchanged from the

         earlier workpaper;

      c. the replacement advertising-expense workpaper and supporting materials add expenses

         and approximately eighty-six pages of invoices and advertising materials that were not

         included in the filing previously deemed complete, without testimony or other

         affirmative support addressing the allowability of each expenditure under

         17.3.350.9(E) NMAC;

      d. the corrections to the calculation of miscellaneous service charges are not reflected in

         revised proposed tariffs, the proposed base-rate revenue requirement, proposed base

         rates, or other potentially affected portions of the Application;

      e. EPE has not provided a revised, executable cost-of-service study showing the

         cumulative effect and order of magnitude of the corrections on the requested New

         Mexico revenue requirement;

      f. EPE has not comprehensively revised or reconciled the affected testimony, exhibits,

         schedules, workpapers, jurisdictional and class cost allocations, rate design, proposed

         tariffs, and discovery responses; and




                                              -5-
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


           g. the Second Errata Notice does not demonstrate that all consequential effects of the

                 identified errors have been located and corrected throughout the filing.9

14.        Doña Ana County similarly states that the late corrections require Staff and intervenors to

determine the effect of revised inputs on EPE’s revenue requirement and cost-of-service

presentation and, as necessary, conduct additional discovery before preparing direct testimony.10

           II.      APPLICABLE PROCEDURAL REQUIREMENTS

15.        The notice and hearing requirements governing Commission proceedings contemplate an

initial filing that identifies the operative proposal and requested relief with sufficient clarity to

permit the Commission and interested persons to understand the matters to be adjudicated and

meaningfully participate in the proceeding.11

16.        1.2.2.37(G)(2) NMAC permits a party to correct “typographical errors, omissions, or other

non-substantial errors” through an errata notice.12

17.        Amendments to pleadings may be made only with leave of the hearing examiner or

presiding officer and upon such conditions as the hearing examiner or presiding officer deems

appropriate. Direct testimony and exhibits likewise may be amended or withdrawn only with leave,

and the hearing examiner or presiding officer may consider the delay or prejudice that would result

from permitting the amendment.13




9

10
     Doña Ana County Response at 3-5.

Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


18.        1.2.2.9 NMAC requires pleadings and documents to comply with applicable filing

requirements and recognizes that a failure to comply with a rule or order may result in rejection of

a pleading or document without prejudice.14

19.        Commission Rule 17.1.3 NMAC reflects the broader procedural principle that a rate

application must be complete and comprehensive, contain full explanations and justifications, and

be presented in a manner designed to minimize unnecessary discovery and permit Staff and

intervenors to test the filing.15

20.        17.1.3.19(C) NMAC specifically contemplates that revisions not requiring a formal

modification will be incorporated into a comprehensive list containing sufficiently detailed

explanations, filed on a date that provides reasonable notice to the parties and precedes Staff and

intervenor direct testimony. Such revisions must be presented as verifiable adjustments to the

original filing.16

21.        The Commission’s discovery rules favor prompt and complete disclosure and authorize

relief necessary to ensure that corrected or late-produced information can be meaningfully

reviewed before testimony is due.17 Consistent with those rules, procedural testimony and motion

deadlines may be vacated, stayed, or reset when necessary to prevent prejudice and permit the fair

development of the record.

     1.2.2.9 NMAC.
15
     17.1.3.6 NMAC.

     17.1.3.19(C) NMAC.
17

Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


           III.   ANALYSIS

22.        The record reflects more than a series of isolated mistakes. Taken together, the original

omissions, the extensive First Errata Notice, the additional corrections in the Second Errata Notice,

the unresolved inconsistencies among the replacement materials, and EPE’s acknowledgment that

further revisions and explanations remain forthcoming have created a level of confusion,

uncertainty, and unfair prejudice against Staff and intervenors that is incompatible with a fair and

orderly proceeding.18

23.        A general rate case must proceed from a filing that is sufficiently complete and accurate to

permit the hearing examiner, Staff, and intervenors to identify and evaluate the applicant’s case.19

That essential foundation is absent here.

24.        In this case, the Hearing Examiner, Staff, and intervenors are unfairly prejudiced by the

requirement that they rely upon a fragmented and shifting application to assess the merits of EPE’s

requests. Being forced to do so creates the risk that testimony, discovery, and briefing will address

different versions of the same schedules or calculations and that a final recommended decision

could rely upon documents that have failed to account for corrections that were not carried through

the filings.

25.        EPE’s indication that the revised cost of service would be filed with rebuttal testimony is

particularly problematic. Staff and intervenors cannot be required to file direct testimony

responding to an incomplete or superseded version of EPE’s case and then receive EPE’s fully

corrected cost of service study only after their testimony has been filed.




18
     See ABCWUA v. NMPRC, 2010-NMSC-013, ¶ 53.
19
     Id.

                                                   -8-
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


26.    The Hearing Examiner recognizes that large and complex filings may contain errors. A

limited errata process serves the legitimate purpose of correcting typographical mistakes,

inadvertent omissions, and other non-substantial defects without unnecessary delay. But that

limited mechanism cannot reasonably accommodate repeated substantive corrections to

foundational documents and warnings that even more corrections are forthcoming.

27.    The Hearing Examiner also recognizes that EPE may ultimately be able to explain or rebut

some of the specific concerns raised by the parties. That possibility does not eliminate the

immediate procedural problem, namely that shortly before the deadline for Staff and intervenor

direct testimony in this extremely complex case, the parties were required to spend their time and

resources, for the second time, attempting to determine which documents and calculations

remained operative, whether prior analyses and discovery responses remained reliable, and what

additional information would be necessary to evaluate EPE’s filing. The Commission and the

Hearing Examiner face the same uncertainty in attempting to manage and ultimately adjudicate

the proceeding.

28.    The present record does not support requiring Staff and intervenors to proceed with direct

testimony under the existing schedule. The Hearing Examiner therefore will afford EPE one

strictly limited opportunity to cure the deficiencies in the Application within this docket. EPE must

file a single, complete, comprehensive Amended Application and supporting documentation.

29.    Section 62-8-7(C) provides that, upon the filing of “a complete application as prescribed

by commission rule proposing new rates,” the Commission may enter upon a hearing concerning

the reasonableness of the proposed rates. If a hearing is necessary, the Commission may suspend

operation of the proposed rates for an initial period not exceeding nine months beyond the date on




                                                -9-
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


which the rates otherwise would become effective and, upon finding that a longer period will be

required, for an additional three months.20

30.       The record developed after the Commission’s April 24, 2026, completeness determination

demonstrates that EPE’s filing contained material omissions and errors and did not provide a

single, complete, internally consistent, and reviewable presentation of EPE’s proposed rates. The

April 24th determination was an interlocutory procedural determination based upon the record then

available and does not require the Hearing Examiner to continue adjudicating a filing that

subsequent disclosures have shown is not reasonably capable of serving as the operative

application.

31.       The deficiencies in EPE’s filing make it impossible to maintain the existing procedural

schedule while preserving Staff’s and the intervenors’ opportunity to investigate and respond

meaningfully to EPE’s operative case. The procedural deadlines established by prior orders

therefore must be vacated or suspended pending the filing and review of the Amended Application.

32.       The Hearing Examiner further finds that the time needed for EPE to prepare and file its

Amended Application, for Staff to review that filing, and for the parties to conduct any necessary

follow-up discovery and prepare responsive testimony should not reduce the time available to the

Commission to evaluate and decide the case. Accordingly, all procedural deadlines in this docket

are tolled, and the procedural schedule shall remain suspended while EPE prepares the Amended

Application and Staff completes its review. If additional time is ultimately needed beyond the

initial statutory suspension period, the Commission may extend that period by up to three months

pursuant to NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-7(C).



20
     NMSA 1978, § 62-8-7(C) (1991).

                                               - 10 -
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


33.     This Order does not determine whether, or to what extent, the time required to cure

deficiencies in a filing previously deemed complete should be excluded in calculating the statutory

suspension period. Nor does it rely upon an implied authority to extend that period beyond the

additional three months expressly authorized by Section 62-8-7(C). The effect of the Amended

Application upon the applicable statutory period, including its proposed effective date and whether

a revised advice notice is required, is reserved pending the Amended Application and an

opportunity for the parties to state their positions.

34.     This Order does not address, resolve, or prejudge the merits of EPE’s substantive requests

or the parties’ respective Motions.

        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:
A.      The procedural schedule established by the Procedural Order issued on April 27, 2026,

including all testimony, prehearing, hearing, and related deadlines established by that Order or any

subsequent procedural order, is VACATED. Those deadlines shall be reset, as appropriate, by

further procedural order.

B.      All pending deadlines for motions or responses to motions are TOLLED pending further

order of the Hearing Examiner.

C.      The evidentiary hearing presently scheduled to commence on September 21, 2026, is

VACATED.

D.      No party shall be required to file testimony or other merits-related submissions until a new

procedural schedule is issued. The vacatur and stay of procedural deadlines ordered herein do not

toll or extend the statutory suspension period applicable to Advice Notice No. 317.

E.      Within twenty-one calendar days after issuance of this Order, EPE shall file an

Amended Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates and a complete replacement filing


                                                 - 11 -
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


package (collectively “Amended Application”). EPE shall file one integrated and comprehensive

Amended Application that supersedes the original Application, the First Errata Notice, the Second

Errata Notice, and all prior replacement or supplemental versions of affected documents.

       1) The Amended Application shall clearly state that it is the single operative version of

           EPE’s affirmative filing in this docket.

       2) EPE shall contemporaneously file a complete set of all testimony, exhibits, schedules,

           workpapers, cost-of-service studies, models, proposed tariffs, rate calculations, and any

           other supporting documents upon which it relies, regardless of whether particular

           documents were previously filed and remain unchanged. EPE shall not incorporate

           prior versions of affected documents by general reference where doing so would require

           Staff, intervenors, or the Hearing Examiner to determine which prior version remains

           operative.

       3) Before filing the Amended Application, EPE shall conduct a comprehensive review

           sufficient to ensure, to the extent it can be reasonably known at that time, that the filing

           does not rely upon future rebuttal testimony, future errata, future replacement exhibits,

           future workpapers, or anticipated discovery supplementation to establish any

           foundational component of EPE’s affirmative case. The Amended Application shall

           contain no unresolved ambiguity as to which testimony, exhibit, schedule, workpaper,

           model, tariff, calculation, or discovery response is operative.

       4) EPE shall file with the Amended Application a comprehensive correction and

           reconciliation matrix. The matrix shall identify every error, omission, correction,

           replacement, or supplementation disclosed in the First Errata Notice, the Second Errata




                                                - 12 -
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


           Notice, discovery responses, pending motions, party correspondence included in the

           record, or EPE’s further internal review.

       5) EPE shall file a verification executed by an authorized officer of the Company stating

           that EPE has undertaken a comprehensive review of the Amended Application and

           supporting materials and that, to the best of the officer’s knowledge after reasonable

           inquiry, the Amended Application is complete, accurate, internally consistent, and not

           known, at that time, to require further material correction or supplementation.

       6) EPE shall also file verifications from each sponsoring witness confirming that the

           witness has reviewed the amended testimony, exhibits, schedules, and workpapers

           sponsored by that witness and that those materials are complete, accurate, internally

           consistent, and consistent with the Amended Application.

       7) EPE shall provide all executable, native-format workpapers and models without

           technical limitations that would prevent Staff and intervenors from reproducing EPE’s

           calculations.

       8) EPE shall contemporaneously supplement all discovery responses that are affected by

           the Amended Application. No prior discovery response shall be treated as current

           merely because EPE does not expressly withdraw it. EPE bears the responsibility to

           determine which prior responses are no longer complete, accurate, or consistent with

           the Amended Application.

F.     Within seven calendar days after EPE files the Amended Application, Staff shall file a

Completeness Report. Staff’s report shall state whether the Amended Application and supporting

materials are sufficiently complete, coherent, internally consistent, and technically usable to permit

the proceeding to continue.

                                                - 13 -
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


G.     In conducting its review, Staff shall consider, at minimum, whether:

       1) EPE filed all materials required by this Order;

       2) the Amended Application identifies one authoritative and operative version of EPE’s

           case;

       3) the correction and reconciliation matrix is complete and usable;

       4) all identified corrections appear to have been carried through affected materials;

       5) the amended cost-of-service study and associated models are complete and executable;

       6) the amended testimony, schedules, workpapers, proposed tariffs, and rate calculations

           are internally consistent;

       7) Staff can trace material adjustments and requested amounts through the filing;

       8) the Amended Application resolves the facial inconsistencies and omissions identified

           in the pending motions and objections;

       9) EPE has adequately supplemented affected discovery responses; and

       10) additional foundational corrections or supplementation appear necessary before Staff

           and intervenors can fairly prepare testimony.

H.     Staff’s review shall be limited to procedural completeness, coherence, internal consistency,

and usability. Staff shall provide any advice or commentary on whether EPE’s substantive requests

are reasonable, lawful, or supported by the weight of the evidence.

I.     Staff may state that particular matters require additional discovery or substantive analysis

without treating those matters as completeness defects, provided the operative filing and

supporting information are sufficiently clear and complete to permit that discovery or analysis to

proceed.




                                              - 14 -
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


J.     If Staff concludes that the Amended Application is complete, coherent, internally

consistent, and sufficiently usable, and the Hearing Examiner agrees, the Hearing Examiner will

issue a new procedural order establishing dates that are consistent with the then-applicable

statutory suspension period, unless the Commission separately extends that period pursuant to

Section 62-8-7(C) NMSA 1978.

       1) The new procedural order will include deadlines and procedures for resolving the CLC

          Motion to Dismiss, the CLC Motion to Compel, the Joint Objection, and any other

          pending motions that remain applicable after review of the Amended Application.

       2) All pending motions shall remain under advisement while the procedural deadlines are

          stayed. No pending motion is denied, granted, or rendered moot by this Order except

          to the extent expressly stated.

       3) The parties shall not be required to supplement or re-brief pending motions unless

          directed by the Hearing Examiner.

       4) After reviewing the Amended Application, the parties may be required to identify

          whether each pending motion remains applicable, has been narrowed, requires

          supplementation, or has become moot.

       5) Discovery already served and responses already provided shall remain part of the

          record and shall be preserved.

       6) Nothing in this Order requires a party to re-serve prior discovery solely because EPE

          files an Amended Application. The Hearing Examiner may establish procedures in the

          new procedural order for adopting, supplementing, revising, or renewing prior

          discovery.




                                              - 15 -
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Tolling Deadlines and Requiring Amended Application Docket No. 25-00082-UT


       7) No party shall be deemed to have waived any discovery objection, request for

           supplementation, motion to compel, confidentiality claim, or other procedural position

           by operation of this Order.

       8) The vacatur and stay of procedural deadlines ordered herein do not relieve EPE of its

           continuing obligation to respond completely and accurately to outstanding discovery

           or to supplement prior responses as required by Commission rules.

K.     This Order affords EPE one opportunity to provide a viable application in this docket. If

EPE fails to file the Amended Application within twenty-one days, fails to comply fully with the

requirements of this Order, or files an Amended Application and supporting materials that do not

provide a complete, coherent, internally consistent, and reviewable basis for further proceedings,

the Hearing Examiner will recommend that the Application be dismissed without prejudice,

requiring EPE to initiate any renewed request for rate relief in a new docket.

L.     Nothing in this Order constitutes a finding concerning the substantive correctness,

reasonableness, or lawfulness of any request, calculation, allocation, expense, rate, tariff, or

accounting treatment proposed by EPE.

M.     This Order is effective immediately.

       ISSUED under the seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on July 16, 2026.

                      NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
